title: Ella Langley sweeps Country Music Awards as Taylor Swift returns from 13-year-absence
summary: Ella Langley and her unstoppable hit Choosin' Texas dominated the Country Music Association Awards on Wednesday at ‌a ceremony that also featured Taylor Swift's first performance at the CMAs in 13…

image.caption: Ella Langley accepts the award for entertainer of the year during the Country Music Association Awards in Nashville on Wednesday. (Mario Anzuoni/Reuters)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Ella Langley and her unstoppable hit Choosin' Texas dominated the Country Music Association Awards on Wednesday at ‌a ceremony that also featured Taylor Swift's first performance at the CMAs in 13 years.
Show pays tribute to late country music legend Parton
Swift, who began her career in country music before finding megastardom in pop, went into the show in Nashville with one nomination for I Knew It, I Knew You from the Toy Story 5 movie soundtrack.

In the night's first ​award, CMA voters chose Choosin' Texas over Swift's entry for single of ​the year. It was one of six awards for Langley, including the event's top honour of entertainer of the year.

"I love this song," the 27-year-old Langley said after winning the single award. "We ​just sat in a room and did our best one afternoon, and it is the ⁠gift that just keeps on giving. ⁠I can't believe this is my life, and what ‌is going on is absolutely insane. I just can't believe it's me that this is happening to."

Choosin' Texas became a cultural phenomenon. It ranked No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart for 27 weeks, breaking a record set by Mariah Carey's perennial holiday hit All I Want for Christmas Is You.
Miranda Lambert, left, and Langley, right, performed their duet Snakeskin Boots during the show. (Mario Anzuoni/Reuters)
Langley ⁠was at a loss for words as she racked up award after award, sweeping the major categories including album and song of the year.

"At this point I'm sick of me," she joked during the last of several acceptance speeches. "This has been ‌the most special night. I could quit tomorrow and have the best career of my life. So thank you."

Winners were chosen by more than 7,000 members of the Country Music Association, a group that includes musicians, songwriters, executives and others in the industry. The gala was broadcast live on ABC and streamed on ​Disney+.
'Dolly gave us her heart'

Midway through the show, Swift sang a mashup of I Knew It, I Knew You and her 2006 country hit Our Song. She wore a red-and-white dress with ⁠bejeweled cowboy boots and was joined onstage by Keith Urban, playing banjo.
Swift took the microphone again to present the ⁠Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award to Brooks & Dunn, a duo known for hits such as Boot Scootin' Boogie.
Taylor Swift returned to the Country Music Association Awards on Wednesday to perform a mashup of I Knew It, I Knew You and her 2006 country hit Our Song. (Mario Anzuoni/Reuters)
"They still approach ⁠their music ⁠with the mischief and excitement of little ​kids just discovering their love for this," Swift said.

The CMAs opened with a tribute to country music legend Dolly Parton, who ​died in August aged 80. ⁠Host Lainey Wilson called Parton "Tennessee's angel" and sang the ballad I Will Always Love You in a duet with Vince Gill.
"She gave us what we all need in a world where there are so many challenges, something that is even more powerful and enduring than her incredible musical legacy," Wilson said.
"Dolly gave us hope. Dolly gave us joy. Dolly gave us her heart."
CMAs host Lainey Wilson paid tribute for the late Dolly Parton, later joining Vince Gill to perform Parton's iconic hit song I Will Always Love You. (Mario Anzuoni/Reuters)
